title: Bolden's repertoire, range and open horn
summary: The blues and other pieces Bolden played, including Tiger Rag, his high range, no mute, and no sheet music.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: What pieces did Bolden play? Do you remember? Did he play a lot of blues or what? Oh, a whole lot of blues.
He played everything. Paddle on the slope. And the other blues. A whole lot of blues. That's what he used to play more.
And he played Careless Love, do you remember?

Yeah, yeah. He played all of them. I believe they say I could admit, but I believe he made that up. He played everything. Every piece was the side. Some of them was out there like you, but he played all that.
Do you remember in those days that anybody played Tiger Rag or that?

Yeah. Tiger Rag. Tiger Rag. Tiger Rag. Well, he used to call it Tiger Rag back then though. No, he used to call it something else, but he played that. He used to call it Tiger too, no one time I remember. The other number he used to play. And they could paddle behind the door, I'm a good man, won't never know, and all that. He could make all kinds of songs. And I never seen him with no music. I don't know if he really did watch, you know. I never seen him with nothing he could play some of that pieces. And he played what these fathers of the Reers could play and what they couldn't play.
How was his range? Did he play up high a good deal or down low? Did he hit a lot of high notes or low or how was, what kind of a song? Bust right on out.

Everything right on out. Up to the top. Never seen him, put his arm like a full thing, you know. I think Marty's tired, you know, he just keep up there too, look around, and he's a man to get ready to go out. The horn.
Did you ever use a mute or anything?

No, I never seen him with nothing like that. Just an open horn. The groove wall, it was upstairs. High. And I'd be on that side by the bottom, by the gym, looking at him. I'd love him just dancing, doing nothing, just standing up, bummer nobody, beat his arm, watch and listen, you know. I'd get off to myself. That joke was, Nick, he was decent. He'd have to put something in here. He looked at the horn and he had the other side of the back.
